Title: BOM request creation can silently write NULL requested_by_id/created_by when called within ~1-2s of login
Repro Steps: Log in as any user; immediately (within ~1-2s) POST a new BOM request.
Expected Result: requested_by_id and created_by are always populated with the acting user's id.
Actual Result: HTTP 201 success, but requested_by_id/created_by are written as NULL when the call happens within ~1-2s of login; always correct with a 2s+ delay.
Evidence: Deterministically reproduced across repeated runs by the API/DB-integrity QA pass: no delay -> always nulled; 2s delay -> never nulled.
Business Impact: A BOM request with no recorded requester is an audit/accountability gap - approval chains and 'who requested this' reporting silently lose attribution for the affected rows.
Reproducibility: High - deterministic given the timing condition, not a rare race.
Suspected Cause: getTmsViewer() (lib/tmsAccess.ts) and tmsBomRequestStore.create()'s separate username->id lookups both momentarily fail to resolve the just-authenticated user right after login.

Title: general_tasks.assignee_id foreign key lacks ON DELETE SET NULL/CASCADE - deleting a user with an assigned task throws a raw DB error
Affected Page/API: Admin user-delete path; general_tasks table FK
Repro Steps: Assign a general task to a user, then attempt to delete that user via the admin user-management flow.
Expected Result: Either the delete is blocked with a clear app-level error, or the task's assignee is cleanly nulled/reassigned, and the user record is removed without a raw DB exception.
Actual Result: Deleting a user with an assigned general task throws a raw SequelizeForeignKeyConstraintError instead of a clean, user-facing app-level error.
Evidence: Found via live UI/UX QA pass while testing /admin/task-assignment; confirmed via the FK definition lacking ON DELETE SET NULL/CASCADE.
Business Impact: An admin attempting to offboard/delete a user with any assigned general task gets an unhandled/ugly error instead of clear guidance - a real admin-workflow usability and offboarding-process risk, not yet confirmed to occur on the production user-delete path specifically (flagged for review).
Reproducibility: Medium - will occur every time this specific combination (user has an assigned general task, admin tries to delete that user) is attempted, not rare.
Suspected Cause: Missing ON DELETE SET NULL/CASCADE (or an app-level pre-check) on the general_tasks.assignee_id foreign key.
Files Likely Involved: db/migrations/ (the general_tasks table's assignee_id FK definition); admin user-delete route handler

Title: /support page fires 2 unnecessary 403 requests on every load for a role that can never access it
User Role: user (Sales) and any role without support-ticket access
Repro Steps: Load /support as a role known to never have access to this module.
Expected Result: The page recognizes up front that this role has no access and does not fire avoidable authenticated requests that are guaranteed to fail.
Actual Result: Page loads to a correct RBAC-denied empty state, but fires 2 separate 403-returning requests on every load before reaching that state.
Evidence: Observed directly during the live UI/UX QA pass.
Business Impact: None functionally - the correct denied state is still shown - but it is unnecessary load/noise on every page visit for roles that will always be denied.
Reproducibility: High - happens on every single load for an unauthorized role.
Suspected Cause: Frontend likely fires its data-fetch calls before/independently of checking the role's module access, rather than short-circuiting first.
Files Likely Involved: Likely the /support page component and its data-fetching hooks.
